title: Best Marketing Strategists (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a marketing strategist: what the strategy should include, what to prepare, what drives the price and the red flags to avoid.
intro: A marketing strategist helps you decide where to focus: which customers, which message, which channels and in what order. A good strategy saves money by stopping you from trying everything at once. Strategy projects disappoint when they end as a long document full of general advice that nobody can act on. This guide helps you get a plan you can actually follow.

faq.q: What should a marketing strategy include?
faq.a: Usually your target customers, your main message and positioning, the channels to use, a simple plan with priorities, a budget split and how you will measure results. It should end with concrete next steps.

faq.q: Will the strategist also run the marketing?
faq.a: Usually not. Strategy is the planning. Running ads, writing content or managing social media are separate services, though some strategists can recommend or coordinate them.

faq.q: How long does a strategy stay useful?
faq.a: The core, your customers and message, can last a long time. Channel plans need regular review, often every quarter, as you learn what works.

faq.q: Do I need a strategy if I am just starting?
faq.a: A short one helps. Even a one-page plan that names your customer, your message and one or two channels to test keeps you focused.

faq.q: What information will the strategist need?
faq.a: Your goals, budget, current customers, past marketing results and competitors. The more real data you share, the more specific the plan can be.
